formats.name: bson
formats.description: Read and write raw BSON files with COPY
formats.comment: Byte-preserving BSON file import and export

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Import or export raw BSON documents using COPY with FORMAT 'bson.bson' (replace the first bson with your attached catalog name). Requires exactly one `BLOB` column, one complete BSON document per row. MODE defaults to 'raw'; typed rows are not supported. Local files only; reads stream in bounded batches. Invalid documents, duplicate keys, truncated files, NULL rows, and oversized documents fail the COPY. MAX_DOCUMENT_SIZE defaults to 16777216 bytes (16 MiB), and may be raised up to 2147483647. Bytes are preserved without decoding/re-encoding. Export preserves source order (use ORDER BY for deterministic ordering), stages batches in shared storage, and atomically replaces the destination only after successful writing. Empty export creates a zero-byte file.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Import or export raw BSON documents using COPY with FORMAT 'bson.bson' (replace the first bson with your attached catalog name). Requires exactly one `BLOB` column, one complete BSON document per row. MODE defaults to 'raw'; typed rows are not supported. Local files only; reads stream in bounded batches. Invalid documents, duplicate keys, truncated files, NULL rows, and oversized documents fail the COPY. MAX_DOCUMENT_SIZE defaults to 16777216 bytes (16 MiB), and may be raised up to 2147483647. Bytes are preserved without decoding/re-encoding. Export preserves source order (use ORDER BY for deterministic ordering), stages batches in shared storage, and atomically replaces the destination only after successful writing. Empty export creates a zero-byte file.

### Import and export

Create the destination table in a writable DuckDB schema, then import a local mongodump document file. Qualify the format by the catalog's ATTACH alias.

```sql
COPY <target_table> FROM '<input_path>' (FORMAT '<catalog>.bson');
COPY (<query_returning_one_blob_column>) TO '<output_path>'
(FORMAT '<catalog>.bson', MODE 'raw');
```

A bad import aborts the statement and reports its filename and document byte offset. A bad export reports its source row and leaves an existing destination intact. COPY accepts one uncompressed file; cloud paths, globs, collection metadata and mongodump archive containers are outside this format. Paths are resolved on the worker's filesystem. MAX_DOCUMENT_SIZE can be raised explicitly for larger documents.
tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
COPY FROM fills the target table's single `BLOB` column, using its name. COPY TO writes the source's single `BLOB` column. DuckDB reports the copied row count. For a target table `docs(doc BLOB)`, the imported columns are:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| doc | BLOB | One complete validated BSON document, with its original bytes. |

The column name follows the target schema; the type must be `BLOB`. Invoke through COPY, not as a table function.
tags.vgi.title: BSON COPY

options.name: mode
options.description: Document representation: 'raw' (default), exactly one BLOB column.

options.name: max_document_size
options.description: Maximum bytes per BSON document, including its prefix; default 16 MiB. Applies to import and export.

formats.name: cbor
formats.description: Bulk import and export of CBOR row files (CBOR Sequence (RFC 8742)), one item per row
formats.comment: Load a CBOR row file (CBOR Sequence (RFC 8742)) into the COPY target table

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Bulk-move whole tables in and out of CBOR data files — the row-file counterpart to the per-blob `decode` scalar. The file is a CBOR Sequence (RFC 8742): one top-level item per row, with no container header or footer, so it appends and streams. The same format name serves both directions, and a file written by one round-trips through the other. The `FORMAT` identifier is scoped by the ATTACH alias, so it reads `<alias>.cbor`:

```sql
COPY (<query>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT '<alias>.cbor');
COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT '<alias>.cbor');
```

With the default `row_format 'map'` each item is a map keyed by column name: self-describing, so on read the columns may appear in any order, a key absent from an item reads as NULL, and extra keys are ignored. `row_format 'array'` frames each row as an array of values in column order — more compact, but positional. Column values encode exactly as the `encode` scalar does (shortest-lossless integers and floats, `BLOB` as a byte string, `TIMESTAMP` as an epoch instant, `LIST` / `STRUCT` / `MAP` as arrays and maps) and decode back onto the COPY target's exact column types. A value that cannot be represented in its target column fails the COPY with a column-qualified message; `ignore_errors true` instead skips unusable rows and warns about skipped data. A decode error discards that file's unreadable remainder and continues with the next source; source-open failures still fail the COPY. Rows are written in source order, so an ordered source query keeps its ordering in the file. On write, `canonical 'core'` (RFC 8949 §4.2.1) or `canonical 'ctap2'` orders map keys deterministically, so the same rows always produce byte-identical output.

**Paths resolve on the worker.** The file is opened by the worker process, so the path is interpreted against its filesystem and working directory — not the SQL client's. That is invisible when DuckDB spawns the worker locally, but a worker in a container or on another host cannot see the caller's paths: use a location both sides agree on (a mounted volume), and prefer absolute paths. A path the worker cannot open is reported with the directory it actually looked in.
tags.vgi.doc_md:

```sql
COPY (<query>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT '<alias>.cbor');
COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT '<alias>.cbor');
```

`row_format 'map'` (the default) keys each row by column name; `row_format 'array'` is positional. On read, `ignore_errors true` skips unusable rows with warnings. A decode error discards that file's unreadable remainder and continues with the next source; source-open failures still fail the COPY. Writes preserve source order. On write, `canonical 'core'` (RFC 8949 §4.2.1) or `canonical 'ctap2'` orders map keys deterministically, so the same rows always produce byte-identical output.

Paths are opened by the **worker** process, so they resolve against its filesystem and working directory rather than the client's — a containerized or remote worker needs a shared location, and absolute paths.
tags.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Export query results to a CBOR row file, one item per row.","sql":"COPY (SELECT 1 AS id, 'alpha' AS name) TO 'events.cbor' (FORMAT 'cbor.cbor')"},{"description":"Export positionally (each row an array in column order) for a more compact file.","sql":"COPY (SELECT 1 AS id, 'alpha' AS name) TO 'events_array.cbor' (FORMAT 'cbor.cbor', row_format 'array')"},{"description":"List the COPY options this format accepts, and the directions it serves.","sql":"SELECT format_name, direction, option_name FROM vgi_copy_formats() WHERE handler = 'cbor_copy' ORDER BY option_name"}]
tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
### Read direction — columns mirror the COPY target

The scan emits exactly the COPY target table's columns, in its declared order and types: DuckDB fixes them from the target and the reader projects each CBOR item onto them, inserting no cast. There is no independent result schema, so the shape below is one worked variant — a target declared `(id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, seen TIMESTAMP)`.

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| id | INTEGER | The item's value for the `id` column — by key name under `row_format 'map'`, by position under `row_format 'array'`. |
| name | VARCHAR | The item's value for the `name` column. A nested value lands as its JSON text. |
| seen | TIMESTAMP | The item's value for the `seen` column, read from an epoch instant. A key absent from the item reads as `NULL`. |
tags.vgi.title: CBOR Row Files (COPY FROM / TO)

options.name: row_format
options.description: How each row is framed as one item: 'map' (default) keys it by column name; 'array' writes the values positionally in column order.

options.name: ignore_errors
options.description: Skip incompatible rows with warnings. On a decode error, discard that file's unreadable remainder and continue with the next source (default false). Source-open failures still fail the COPY.

options.name: canonical
options.description: Deterministic map-key ordering to apply: 'core' (RFC 8949 §4.2.1) or 'ctap2'. Unset keeps ciborium's shortest-form output with keys in column order.

formats.name: atom
formats.description: Export SQL rows to a atom feed document using COPY TO
formats.comment: Export feed items to a worker-local file, preserving query order.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Export atom using COPY TO a worker-local file. Source columns are matched by feed_items column names and types. title and link options are required; RSS also requires description. Optional language and author describe the feed. Use ORDER BY to choose item order. Missing item IDs are generated deterministically; Atom dates default to the export time.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## Generate a atom feed

Export atom using COPY TO a worker-local file. Source columns are matched by feed_items column names and types. title and link options are required; RSS also requires description. Optional language and author describe the feed. Use ORDER BY to choose item order. Missing item IDs are generated deterministically; Atom dates default to the export time.

### Input and output

Alias and cast source columns to the item schema; subsets are supported. This is a sink with no result columns. DuckDB reports the COPY row count. Every item needs title, summary, or content; Atom requires a title. Empty input produces a valid empty feed.

### Example

```sql
COPY (SELECT 'First post' AS title, 'https://example.com/1' AS link)
TO '/tmp/posts.feed' (FORMAT 'feed.atom', title 'Posts', link 'https://example.com', description 'Recent posts');
```

### Limits

Only worker-local destinations are supported. Buffered input and encoded output are limited to 64 MiB, and exports to one million items. The destination is replaced after successful encoding.
tags.vgi.title: COPY atom feed

options.description: Required feed title

options.name: link
options.description: Required absolute HTTP or HTTPS home-page URL

options.name: description
options.description: Feed description; required for RSS

options.name: language
options.description: Feed language code

options.name: author
options.description: Feed author name; defaults to the feed title for Atom

formats.name: auto
formats.description: Import RSS, Atom, or JSON Feed items from a URL or file using COPY FROM
formats.comment: Import feed items from an HTTP(S) URL or a worker-local file; columns map by name.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Import auto feed items using COPY FROM an HTTP(S) URL or worker-local file. Target columns must be a subset of feed_items columns with matching names and types. timeout_ms defaults to 15000; max_items defaults to 0 (all items). Documents over 64 MiB or over one million items are rejected.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## Import feed items

Import auto feed items using COPY FROM an HTTP(S) URL or worker-local file. Target columns must be a subset of feed_items columns with matching names and types. timeout_ms defaults to 15000; max_items defaults to 0 (all items). Documents over 64 MiB or over one million items are rejected.

### Column mapping

The destination table chooses the output schema. Use any subset of the item columns, in any order, with matching types. Dates are plain `TIMESTAMP`; categories are `VARCHAR[]`. Unknown columns and incompatible types are errors.

### Example

```sql
CREATE TABLE headlines (title VARCHAR, link VARCHAR);
COPY headlines FROM 'https://hnrss.org/frontpage' (FORMAT 'feed.auto', timeout_ms 5000);
```

Local file paths refer to the worker's filesystem, including for remote workers.
tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
The COPY destination selects any subset and order of these columns.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| seq | BIGINT | Zero-based position in the feed. |
| guid | VARCHAR | Item ID, or empty when absent. |
| title | VARCHAR | Item title. |
| link | VARCHAR | Item URL. |
| published | TIMESTAMP | Publish time in UTC; NULL when unavailable. |
| updated | TIMESTAMP | Update time in UTC; NULL when unavailable. |
| author | VARCHAR | Author name or email. |
| categories | VARCHAR[] | Category names; empty list when absent. |
| summary | VARCHAR | Item summary. |
| content | VARCHAR | Full item content. |
tags.vgi.title: COPY auto feed

options.name: timeout_ms
options.description: HTTP timeout in milliseconds

options.name: max_items
options.description: Maximum items; zero imports all items up to the safety limit

formats.name: fixed
formats.description: Read a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file into the COPY target table (the COPY-FROM counterpart of read_fixed)
formats.comment: Load a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file into the COPY target table

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Load a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file straight into a DuckDB table — the COPY-FROM counterpart of read_fixed. It is invoked as a COPY statement (not called directly):

```sql
COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed', spec '<layout>');
```

The format name is catalog-qualified by the ATTACH name (e.g. 'fixed.fixed'). Each record is decoded per the `spec` option (a Perl/Python `unpack` template, a JSON field list, or a COBOL copybook; auto-detected unless `format` is given) and the decoded columns are assigned to the COPY target table's columns BY POSITION and cast to each target column's type, so the spec must produce the same number of columns in the same order. Options are named: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding` ('ascii'/'ebcdic'), `framing` ('newline'/'fixed'/'rdw'/'rdw_blocked'), `record_length` (bytes, 'fixed' framing only), plus `endpoint`/`region`/`url_style`/`use_ssl` for `s3://` sources. `path` may be local, `s3://`, or `http(s)://`. Use it to ingest mainframe or legacy flat-file data into an existing table without a read_fixed call.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Load a fixed-width file into a table:

```sql
COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed', spec '<layout>');
```

Decoded columns map to the target table's columns by position (cast to each type). Named options: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding`, `framing`, `record_length`, and S3 overrides. The COPY-FROM counterpart of `read_fixed`.
tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
`copy_fixed` is invoked through `COPY <table> FROM '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed', …)`, not as a table function, so it returns **no result set of its own**. The rows decoded from the file are inserted into the COPY **target table**, and DuckDB reports the number of rows loaded as the statement's `Count`. The materialized columns are therefore the target table's own columns — each decoded field is mapped to a target column **by position** and cast to that column's type, so the `spec` must produce the same number of columns, in the same order, as the table.

For a target table `accounts(name VARCHAR, qty INTEGER)` loaded with the spec `name:A10 qty:9(5)`, the loaded columns are:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | VARCHAR | The target column populated from the first decoded field (bytes 0–9). |
| `qty` | INTEGER | The target column populated from the second decoded field, cast from the 5-digit value. |
tags.vgi.title: Load Fixed-Width File (COPY FROM)

options.name: spec
options.description: The record layout to decode each row with: a Perl/Python `unpack` template, a JSON field list, or a COBOL copybook. The decoded columns are assigned to the COPY target table's columns by position, so the spec must produce the same number of columns in the same order (each cast to the target column's type).

options.name: format
options.description: Force how `spec` is interpreted: 'template', 'json', or 'copybook'. Omit to auto-detect.

options.name: encoding
options.description: Byte encoding of the file: 'ascii' (the default) or 'ebcdic' (CP037).

options.name: framing
options.description: How records are delimited: 'newline' (the default), 'fixed', 'rdw', or 'rdw_blocked'.

options.name: record_length
options.description: The length of each record in BYTES; used only for 'fixed' framing. Defaults to the length implied by the layout `spec`.

options.name: compression
options.description: Input compression: 'auto' (the default — detect gzip/zstd from the file's magic bytes, else read raw), 'none', 'gzip', or 'zstd'. Applies to local and cloud paths alike; decompression happens before framing/decoding.

options.name: max_decompressed_bytes
options.description: Safety cap on total DECOMPRESSED bytes per file (a decompression-bomb backstop; default 16 GiB). Only applies to gzip/zstd input. Raise it to load a legitimately huge compressed file.

options.name: endpoint
options.description: Custom S3 endpoint for an `s3://` source (e.g. MinIO/R2 'host:9000'); overrides any endpoint from a CREATE SECRET.

options.name: region
options.description: AWS region for an `s3://` source. Overrides the region from a CREATE SECRET.

options.name: url_style
options.description: S3 addressing for an `s3://` source: 'path' (path-style, e.g. MinIO) or 'vhost'.

options.name: use_ssl
options.description: Whether to use TLS for an `s3://` source's custom endpoint (default true).

formats.name: fixed_out
formats.description: Write the COPY source out to a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file (the COPY-TO counterpart of write_fixed)
formats.comment: Write the COPY source out to a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file

tags.vgi.doc_llm:
Write a query or table out to a fixed-width / flat-file / COBOL-copybook file — the COPY-TO counterpart of write_fixed. It is invoked as a COPY statement (not called directly):

```sql
COPY (<query>|<table>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed_out', spec '<layout>');
```

The writer uses a DISTINCT format name 'fixed.fixed_out' (catalog-qualified by the ATTACH name) because the VGI SDK advertises FROM and TO as separate formats. Each input column is matched to a layout field BY NAME, encoded to record bytes per the `spec` option (a Perl/Python `unpack` template, a JSON field list, or a COBOL copybook; auto-detected unless `format` is given), framed per `framing`, and written to `<path>` (overwritten if it exists). Options are named: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding` ('ascii'/'ebcdic'), `framing` ('newline'/'fixed'/'rdw'/'rdw_blocked'), plus `endpoint`/`region`/`url_style`/`use_ssl` for `s3://` destinations. NOTE: CREATE SECRET credentials are NOT forwarded on the COPY-TO path — use named S3 overrides, ambient credentials, or write_fixed for secret-backed cloud writes.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
Write a relation to a fixed-width file:

```sql
COPY (<query>|<table>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed_out', spec '<layout>');
```

Input columns map to layout fields by name. Named options: `spec` (required), `format`, `encoding`, `framing`, and S3 overrides. The COPY-TO counterpart of `write_fixed`.
tags.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
`copy_to_fixed` is invoked through `COPY (<query>|<table>) TO '<path>' (FORMAT 'fixed.fixed_out', …)`, not as a table function, so it returns **no result set of its own**. The COPY source rows are encoded to fixed-width records and written to `<path>` (overwritten if it exists); each input column is matched to a layout field **by name** before encoding. DuckDB reports only a single value — the number of rows written:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Count` | BIGINT | The number of source rows written to the file, reported by DuckDB as the `COPY … TO` statement's result. |
tags.vgi.title: Write Fixed-Width File (COPY TO)

formats.name: pmtiles
formats.description: COPY ... TO format that encodes rows with a GEOMETRY column as a PMTiles vector tileset
formats.comment: Vector tiles (MVT) in a PMTiles v3 archive

tags.vgi.doc_llm: A COPY TO format, not a table function: use it as FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles' in a COPY ... TO statement whose destination is a local .pmtiles path. Each row is a feature. The `GEOMETRY` column must be WGS84 lon/lat (or EPSG:3857). A `VARCHAR` column named `layer` (or `layer_column`) names each row's layer, so one COPY can write several layers via UNION ALL; without it every row goes to `layer` (default: the file name). A column named `feature_id` (or `id_column`) becomes the feature id, and a column named `properties` holding JSON objects is expanded into attributes, so read_tiles output can be written back. Every other column becomes an attribute (`VARCHAR`, numbers, `BOOLEAN`; dates as ISO text; lists and structs as JSON text); NULLs are omitted. Options: minzoom/maxzoom (default 0/14); minzoom_column/maxzoom_column for per-feature zoom ranges; simplify and buffer (pixels of a 256-pixel tile); extent (4096); max_tile_bytes (500000: fails rather than dropping features); max_tiles; name, description, attribution. ORDER BY sets drawing order. COPY reports the number of rows written.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## COPY ... TO (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles')

Encode a query's rows as Mapbox Vector Tiles in a PMTiles archive. One row is one feature; a `layer` column puts rows in different layers of the same tiles, so a single COPY of a `UNION ALL` writes a whole multi-layer basemap.
tags.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Write two cities as a one-layer tileset (zoom 0 to 8)", "sql": "COPY (SELECT 'cities' AS layer, name, population, ST_Point(lon, lat) AS geometry FROM (VALUES ('Rome', 2800000, 12.5, 41.9), ('Paris', 2100000, 2.35, 48.86)) t(name, population, lon, lat)) TO 'cities.pmtiles' (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles', maxzoom 8)"}, {"description": "Re-tile every layer of an existing tileset into a new archive", "sql": "COPY (SELECT layer, feature_id, properties, geometry FROM mvt.main.read_tiles('test/fixtures/sample.pmtiles')) TO 'sample-copy.pmtiles' (FORMAT 'mvt.pmtiles', maxzoom 4, name 'sample copy')"}]

formats.name: x12
formats.description: Import and export complete X12 segment rows through the catalog's COPY format.

tags.vgi.doc_llm: Import and export X12 with the alias-scoped x12 COPY format. FROM emits the complete read_x12 schema. TO consumes ordered segment_id, elements, element_separator, and segment_terminator columns. Paths are worker-local. The writer validates complete ASCII envelopes and publishes only after validation; recalculate_counts updates trailer counts without changing control numbers. Use read_x12 for ordinary SELECT queries.
tags.vgi.doc_md:
## X12 COPY format

The registered handler is invoked by DuckDB's COPY machinery. It cannot be called directly as a table function. Discover the alias-scoped format using the example query.

**Import.** Create the destination table from the schema of `read_x12(input)` with zero rows, then import a worker-local file or glob. Column names, order, and types must match. Reads retain malformed segments for inspection and materialize the input in memory.

**Export.** Supply the four named columns `segment_id`, `elements`, `element_separator`, and `segment_terminator`, ordered by document and segment index. Other columns are informational. ISA11 and ISA16 preserve repetition and component delimiters. Empty element strings are retained; NULL values are rejected.

**Validation and publication.** The writer checks ASCII text, fixed-width ISA, envelope nesting, counts, and control matches across batches. The explicit `recalculate_counts` option updates SE01/GE01/IEA01 only. A same-directory temporary file replaces the target after validation completes; failure preserves the old target. Empty input writes an empty file. This is structural validation; transaction-specific content rules remain outside scope. Formatting whitespace is normalized. EDIFACT and binary payloads are unsupported. See the repository README for the complete edit-and-export workflow.
tags.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Discover the X12 COPY format, supported directions, ordering, and options.","sql":"SELECT DISTINCT format_name, direction, ordered, option_name FROM vgi_copy_formats() WHERE handler = 'copy_x12' ORDER BY format_name, option_name;"}]
